what_happened: On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy steered left out of its lane, away from the recorded path that stays straight. It cut into the left lane next to actor 41, which was alongside it, and hit that vehicle with its front at 7.7 s.

On a multi-lane freeway, the policy's planned path (orange) kept bending left, away from the recorded route (green), even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. At 7.7 s the ego cut into the left lane and its front hit actor 41, a white car in that lane that was nearly beside it.

On a multi-lane highway the route command was RIGHT, but the ego's path veered left toward the next lane. Actor 41 had come up alongside on the left and moved ahead, and the ego, at about 4.6 m/s, drifted about 1.8 m left of the recorded path and hit 41's rear-right corner with its front.

On a multi-lane highway with no lead vehicle close ahead (gap of about 46 m or more), the ego braked hard for no clear reason, from 20 m/s to about 9 m/s, and drifted left. It ended up 1.3 m off the recorded path, and its front-left corner hit actor 1, which was driving alongside it in the adjacent left lane. The route command had just changed to RIGHT. The later rear-end contact most likely came from the unexpected braking.

On an open highway with nothing close ahead (lead gap 44–53 m), the ego braked hard for no clear reason, slowing from 23.7 to 7 m/s, and drifted left toward the lane line. Actor 1, coming up from behind in the left lane, was beside it by then, and at 7.6 s the ego's front-left corner hit actor 1's side. The ego was 9.4 m behind where the human car was at that moment.

On an open highway with no lead within about 46 m, the policy braked hard for no visible reason (20.6 to 9.5 m/s) while drifting left across its lane line. Its front clipped actor 1, a car in the adjacent left lane that the slowing ego had let come alongside. The heavy braking probably also led to the later rear contact.

On a straight multi-lane highway with no lead vehicle within ~46 m, the policy braked hard for no clear reason, slowing from 20 to 9 m/s while the recorded human kept speed. At the same time its path drifted left across the lane line, so its front-left corner hit the rear-right of actor 1, which had been travelling alongside in the left lane and was now ahead because the ego had slowed.

After handoff on a clear multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard for no reason (23.7 → 6.9 m/s; the nearest lead was more than 43 m ahead) and drifted left off the recorded path toward the adjacent lane. Actor 1, which had been just behind on the left, came up alongside, and the ego's front-left corner made contact with it; the rear contact came after.

The ego was following vehicle 12 at about 7 m in slow traffic. It then steered left toward the next lane, which vehicle 56 was occupying right beside it, and its front struck 56 while it was halfway across the lane line. The route command had just changed to RIGHT, so the move was the wrong way as well as unsafe.

The ego was going straight in highway traffic, closing on a slowing blue pickup (actor 5) in its lane, which went from 12.8 m ahead to 5.7 m at handoff (4.7 s) at about 9.3 m/s. The policy braked to 7.6 m/s but front-ended the pickup 0.5 s after taking over. The ego was only 0.1 m off the recorded human path, so the closing situation was largely inherited from the replay.

The ego was following car 12 in its lane at about 5 m/s. Even though the command had switched to RIGHT, it planned and steered left into the next lane and drove its front into car 56, which was travelling alongside slightly ahead in that lane. The human driver stayed right, so the ego ended up about 1.3 m off the recorded path.

The ego was following actor 12 in its lane on a multi-lane arterial. Although the route command switched to RIGHT, the policy's planned path (orange) swerved left toward the adjacent lane, and the ego's front ran into actor 56 there, which was slightly ahead in that lane.

On a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT, the ego was closing fast on the slowing blue pickup (actor 5) in its own lane, and the gap shrank from 16.8 m to 5.7 m by handoff at 4.7 s. The policy braked from 9.3 to 7.6 m/s, which was not enough, and the ego's front hit the pickup 0.5 s after handoff. It was also rear-ended at some point.

The ego was going straight on a busy multi-lane road and closing fast on a blue pickup (actor 5) ahead in its lane. The gap shrank from 12.8 m to 5.7 m while the ego held about 9.5 m/s. The policy took over at 4.7 s, already inside that closing situation, and braked from 9.3 to 7.6 m/s, which was not enough: its front hit the pickup at 5.2 s. The ego was within 0.1 m of the human's recorded path, and an actor also struck its rear at some point.
